public_rationale: The financial core is substantially corroborated: Reuters reports OpenAI lost about USD 5 billion in 2024, and Anthropic's later filing reports a USD 8.3 billion 2024 GAAP net loss. Those records use different bases and do not establish the entire claim as contracted. The assertion that no startup's story is comparable supplies no testable dimensions. The compound claim remains unresolved; this is not a finding that either company was profitable.
limitations: OpenAI's detailed accounting adjustments are unavailable in the cited report.
Anthropic's audited figure includes substantial noncash fair-value changes.
The historical-comparison clause is not independently adjudicable without a defined comparison.
Evidence published after the post is used only for the historical period and was available before the evaluation cutoff.

our_interpretation: The monetary clause means each company separately incurs annual losses of at least USD 2 billion after accounting for revenue.
Use calendar 2024, the latest completed annual period before publication. The nearby 2025 projection is not treated as a realized annual result.
The surrounding discussion relies on reported private-company estimates, so the contract basis is estimate; no GAAP or other accounting standard is asserted.
After revenue is read as net loss rather than spending, financing or cash burn.
No dimensions of similarity are given for startup stories. Annual losses alone cannot establish or disprove the entire historical comparison.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable reported estimates establish at least USD 2 billion of realized annual net loss for each company in 2024. Supporting the entire compound claim would additionally require a defined, defensible historical comparison.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable evidence establishes that at least one company's 2024 annual net loss was below USD 2 billion. A historical comparison can contradict the broader clause only under explicitly specified dimensions of similarity.
